instruction: Identify all slides in the presentation that contain the placeholder text '<number>' and create a document called 'numbered_slides.docx' on the Desktop listing these slide numbers (e.g., 'Slide 4', 'Slide 5', etc.).

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey("ctrl", "s"); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Variation 4: Task requires finding slides with '<number>' placeholder text. Verified from PowerPoint: Slides 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 21, 25, 26, and 28 contain '<number>' text. The evaluator checks if the document lists these slide numbers in the format 'Slide #'.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly extracts docx file content from the expected location (/home/user/Desktop/numbered_slides.docx)
Getter logic (docx_lines) properly reads the Word document and extracts text lines using python-docx library
Metric logic (slide_numbers) correctly parses slide numbers using flexible regex pattern '[Ss]lide\s*#?\s*(\d+)' that matches 'Slide 4', 'Slide #4', 'slide 4', etc.
Expected slides [4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 21, 25, 26, 28] match the metadata explanation and actual presentation content
Postconfig correctly activates the document window and saves it (Ctrl+S) before reading, ensuring file freshness
Partial credit scoring is semantically correct: found_count / total_expected provides proportional score
All instruction requirements are verified: file name, location, content format, and specific slide numbers
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The static warning about 'dict' vs 'Dict' type hint is cosmetic (Python 3.9+ accepts 'dict') and doesn't affect runtime behavior
